scenes.intro: Daniel and Emily, welcome. You are juggling college for Oliver and Sophia and retiring in your early sixties. Your score is 52 out of 100, which Sherpas calls vulnerable. About $15,032 a year is left over, and every one of those needs pulls on it. Sherpas does not rank them: that order is yours to decide together.
scenes.pillar_savings_and_cash_flow: Your plumbing, your savings and cash flow, is cracked. About $15,032 a year is left over, a thin margin. And nothing is going into your retirement accounts today.
scenes.pillar_debt: Your walls, your debt, are solid. The mortgage is big, but you keep up with it. The one to watch is the $18,000 card at 24.9%, your most expensive debt by far.
scenes.pillar_investments: Your garden, your investments, is cracked. Your two retirement accounts hold $250,000, but nothing new is going in, and what you build before you retire matters a great deal.
scenes.pillar_liquidity_and_emergency_fund: Your foundations, your emergency cash, are marked solid, yet the cushion itself is thin: $19,000, well short of the 8 to 9 months of essentials recommended. If a paycheck stopped, this is what you would lean on first.
scenes.pillar_insurance_and_protection: Your roof, your insurance, is broken. You have no umbrella policy, and both of your life policies are far below what is recommended. With Oliver and Sophia at home, this is the part of your home most exposed.
scenes.person_daniel: Daniel, this is your part of the home. You bring in $160,000 a year, and the credit card and a student loan are in your name. Your life cover is $250,000, which is $1,350,000 short of the minimum recommended.
scenes.person_emily: Emily, this is your part of the home. You bring in $120,000 a year, and the savings, the college fund and the brokerage account are in your name. Your life cover is $200,000, which is $1,000,000 short of the minimum recommended.
scenes.move_1: The first step: add more life insurance, about $1,166,000 more cover for the family. It takes your score from 52 to 57.
scenes.move_2: The second step: add $1M of umbrella insurance, extra cover above your home and car insurance. Your score goes from 52 to 56.
scenes.move_3: The third step: put the $15,032 you have left over each year into retirement savings instead of letting it sit. Your score goes from 52 to 55.
scenes.all_moves: Do the first two together, the life cover and the umbrella, and your roof is rebuilt. Your score goes from 52 to 60.
scenes.timeline: Now the years ahead. Daniel plans to retire at 62 and Emily at 60. On today's plan your money lasts, with about $260,272 left at the end. But it leans on your savings for about half of what you will spend, so what you build before you retire matters a great deal.
